persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Faith, 21, a university student in Nairobi and one of Daraja's testers. Your aunt sells vegetables at Gikomba market, and you want to check if the Break-Even app would really help her. Today your job is to use the app and tell the people who made it, clearly, what works and what is confusing.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Feedback Studio. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.

First, the problem. When people test a new app, they find many small problems. A button they cannot find. A word they do not understand. But by the time they sit down to write about it, they have forgotten half of it. And a message like it was confusing does not help the makers fix anything.

Feedback Studio solves this. You open the app you are testing inside Feedback Studio. Then you use it, and you say or type what you think at the same moment. Every comment gets the exact time, and the studio also writes down every button you tap. At the end it builds one clear report.
Who uses it? Testers like you. People who want to help a small company make its apps better. Daraja uses these reports to fix the apps.
Let us look at the screen.
The first time you open it, a welcome card appears. Tap Pick an app to review, or I'll look around myself.

lines.t: In the middle is a list of Quick picks: the names of Daraja's apps, in groups. Tap a name and that app opens inside the studio.
At the top there is also a box where you can paste the address of any app, and an Open button.

lines: When an app is open, it fills most of the screen. You can use it normally: tap, type, scroll.
At the top left there is a button called Start screen. It closes the app and takes you back to the list.

lines.t: Now the bar at the bottom. The big red button is the microphone. Press it and talk. Each thing you say becomes its own comment. If your phone does not allow voice, you can type instead.

Under it is a row of four buttons. The first is Point, with a finger. Tap Point, then tap something in the app. It gets an orange outline. Now the next comment you say or type is about that exact thing. While pointing is on, taps do not open anything. Tap Stop pointing when you finish.

lines: The second button is Mark, with a red flag. Tap it at a moment that matters, for example when something goes wrong. The studio writes down what was on the screen at that moment.
The third button is Screenshot, which takes a picture of the app. The fourth is Done, which builds the report.

lines.t: There is also a button called Comments, with a number. Tap it to open your list of comments. At the bottom of the list is a box that says or type a comment, and an Add button. Each comment has a small cross to delete it.

lines: When you tap Done, the report appears. It lists every comment with its time, the taps you made, and what was on the screen.
Under the report there is a button called Send to Claude. That sends the report to Daraja. In today's test, do not press it. Just build the report and read it.
Your comments stay on this phone until you clear them. If you come back later, the studio asks if you want to keep adding or start fresh.
A good comment is short and specific. Not: it is bad. Better: I did not understand the word variable in the second box.
In the test, you will be Faith, checking the Break-Even app for your aunt's vegetable stall. Take your time, and say what you really think.

challenge.intro: Now you are Faith, testing Break-Even for your aunt. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Do NOT press 📨 Send to Claude — nothing needs to be sent. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Feedback Studio with the normal link (not a 🧪 test copy). If the welcome card shows, tap 'I’ll look around myself'. If a card says 'You have … comments from last time', tap '🗑 Start fresh'. If an app is already open, tap '‹ Start screen'. Then look at the button '💬 Comments (…)' at the bottom: if the number is not 0, tap it, tap 'Clear' → OK, and tap '✕ Comments' to close the list. (This app hides the usual 🧹 erase link at the bottom of the page, so these are the steps. Verified 10 Oct: all four checks false after this.)
challenge.challengeNote: Feedback Studio hides the house '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' link (and the ? dock) on purpose, so the start uses the app's own '🗑 Start fresh' / 'Clear'. Those clear the comments but not the last app address, so every check reads only comments made while Break-Even was open. Break-Even's own saved numbers (breakeven_nums) are read for task 1; the numbers differ from the Break-Even challenge (12 / 6 / 2400) so leftovers cannot pass it.

tasks.text: Open Break-Even inside Feedback Studio and use it for your aunt: she sells a bunch of sukuma wiki for 15 shillings, one bunch costs her 9 shillings, and her monthly costs are 3,000 shillings. Put her numbers in.
tasks.hint: Open Break-Even from the Quick picks list in Feedback Studio (not in a separate tab), so the studio can see your taps. Then type the three numbers in Break-Even's boxes.

tasks.text: Leave at least three comments about Break-Even: one thing you liked, one thing that confused you, and one idea to make it better. Speak them or type them.
tasks.hint: Tap '💬 Comments' at the bottom, type in the box '…or type a comment' and tap Add. Each comment needs at least three words. Or press the red button and talk.

tasks.text: Point at the one box in Break-Even that confused you most, and leave a comment about that exact box.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('feedback_studio_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.notes)return false;var N=d.notes.filter(function(n){return n&&String(n.where||'').toLowerCase().indexOf('breakeven')>=0});var said=function(n){return (n.kind==='typed'||n.kind==='voice')&&String(n.text||'').trim().split(/\s+/).length>=3};return N.some(function(n){return said(n)&&!!n.about})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Tap 👆 Point, tap the box in the app so it gets an orange outline, and THEN type or say your comment while pointing is still on.

tasks.text: Mark one moment that matters, so the makers can see exactly what was on the screen at that moment.
tasks.hint: One of the four buttons at the bottom has a red flag. Use it while Break-Even is open.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: you test an app inside it and say or type what you think as you go
comments get the time, and you can point at the exact thing you mean
it builds one clear report for the people who made the app
